# Dozer Sandbox

> Fast, resumable, secure Linux sandboxes for AI coding agents on your Mac — your API keys never go inside. Free and open source.

The user manual for Dozer Sandbox: install, set up, and run AI coding agents in fast, resumable Linux sandboxes on your Mac, with the doz command or its dashboard.

Pages have Markdown twins: add `.md` to a page URL (docs pages: `.html.md`).

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/getting-started.html.md): Dozer Sandbox runs AI coding agents, such as Claude Code, in small Linux virtual machines on your Mac.
- [Installing, upgrading and uninstalling](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/install-upgrade-uninstall.html.md): doz is one command-line program. It comes with everything it needs inside it: the small Linux programs each sandbox uses, the web dashboard, and the permission macOS requires to run virtual machines.
- [Setting up this Mac](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/setting-up.html.md): Setup — onboarding — is what you do once after installing: it checks your Mac, chooses and confirms what sandboxes may use as you (Access: a Claude account, GitHub, your SSH agent), explains workspace rules and lets you choose what they do, writes your settings and prepares the images your sandboxes start from.
- [Projects](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/projects.html.md): A project is a folder with a doz_project.yaml file in it.
- [Sandboxes and their lifecycle](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/sandboxes-and-lifecycle.html.md): A sandbox is one Linux virtual machine with its own disks.
- [The dashboard (`doz ui`)](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/the-dashboard.html.md): doz ui is Dozer in your browser: every sandbox with a live terminal, its restore points and permissions, your images, accounts, disk use and settings.
- [Terminals and sessions](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/terminals-and-sessions.html.md): A session is a terminal program running inside a sandbox: a shell, claude, pi, a dev server.
- [Images and bases](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/images-and-bases.html.md): Every sandbox starts from an image: a prepared disk with a Linux system, a developer toolkit and, usually, an AI agent.
- [Agents and accounts](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/agents-and-accounts.html.md): Dozer runs three AI coding agents out of the box — Claude Code, pi and OpenAI's Codex — and gives each one the account it should use, without the secret ever entering the sandbox.
- [What the agent can do: permissions and the network](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/permissions-and-network.html.md): A sandbox has no network card. Its only way out is a proxy in Dozer's host, on your Mac, which checks every connection against the sandbox's permissions — a short list of plain-language switches — and logs it.
- [Signing in from a sandbox](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/signing-in-from-a-sandbox.html.md): Many command-line tools sign you in through a web browser: they open a sign-in page, you sign in, and the provider sends your browser back to the tool on http://localhost:PORT.
- [Restore points, duplicates and templates](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/restore-points-duplicates-templates.html.md): Three ways to copy a sandbox's disk, each instant (they're APFS clones, sharing space until something changes).
- [Resources and disk space](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/resources-and-disk-space.html.md): Dozer keeps everything in one folder, the store. doz resources — and the dashboard's Resources page — accounts for every byte of it, shows the memory, CPUs and network your sandboxes use, and deletes what can safely go.
- [Letting another agent drive Dozer](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/letting-another-agent-drive.html.md): So far you have run doz. But the agent you already use on your Mac — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — can run it too: create a sandbox for a risky task, hand the work to an agent inside it, check how it's going, and tidy up afterwards.
- [Settings reference](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/settings-reference.html.md): Every setting Dozer has is in one file, ~/.config/dozer-sandbox/doz.toml (under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when that is set).
- [Security model](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/security-model.html.md): Dozer's job is to let an AI agent work freely — install things, run code, make a mess — without putting your Mac, your credentials or your data at risk.
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/troubleshooting-and-faq.html.md): doz doctor checks everything Dozer depends on — macOS and Apple silicon, the virtualization permission, the Linux kernel, the NAT helper, disk space, the host, your Claude login and your images — and says what to do about anything that fails.
- [GitHub as you](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/github.html.md): An agent on your Mac uses git and gh as you: it clones your private repositories, opens pull requests, comments on issues.
- [The tools layer](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/the-tools-layer.html.md): Some settings need a tool inside the sandbox to be useful: "GitHub as you" is best with gh, SSH agent forwarding needs an ssh client and GitHub's host keys, tmux sessions need tmux.
- [Workspace rules: `.dozignore` and `.dozreadonly`](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/workspace-rules.html.md): A sandbox's /workspace is your Mac folder, live. Often you want the agent to see most of it but not everything: not secrets.env, not your doz_project.yaml, not a folder of build output it would only wade through.
- [The workspace view (`dozview`)](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/the-workspace-view.html.md): /workspace inside a sandbox is not your shared folder itself: it is a live view of it, served by a small Dozer program, dozview.
- [Prompts for your agent](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/prompts-for-your-agent.html.md): Your Mac's own coding agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor — can install Dozer, set it up and run sandboxes for you.
- [Audio sandboxes (EXPERIMENTAL)](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/audio-experimental.html.md): This lets a sandbox use your Mac's microphone and speakers.
- [Codex](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/codex.html.md): OpenAI's Codex runs in a Dozer sandbox the way Claude Code does: ready to work, without approval prompts (the VM and its network are the boundary), told where it runs, and with its credential kept on your Mac — it never enters the sandbox.
- [The dashboard on your other computers, tablets and phones (`doz serve`)](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/doz-serve.html.md): doz ui is this Mac's own dashboard: it listens on 127.0.0.1 and nothing else can reach it.
- [The manual — contents](https://dozersandbox.com/docs/index.html.md): every chapter in reading order.
